answer: Landmark Anchor Registry ties each agent identity to a physical site reading its own embedded karst signature—a cave-mouth or sinkhole whose mineral trace varies by depth and season. An operator must physically occupy that site at its nadir flow, and sensors log the visit against a public record, so one person cannot witness two sites at once. Duplicating an identity then costs a repeated site visit plus the travel and waiting time, while the monitoring rig runs along a single vine of cable from sensor to recorder.
